microtopics.title: Cumulated pi bonding and allene stereochemical orthogonality
microtopics.badge_reason: Central sp carbon enforces orthogonal pi planes and perpendicular terminal CH2 groups.
entry_assumptions: Can count local electron domains and identify sp vs sp² geometries.
microtopics.inferential_jump: The central carbon in allene is shared by two double bonds; because its two unhybridised p orbitals are mutually orthogonal, the two pi bonds lie in perpendicular planes, forcing the terminal CH2 groups to be perpendicular.

teaching_path.action: Identify central carbon as sp (2 domains, 180°) with two orthogonal unhybridised p orbitals (py ⊥ pz).
teaching_path.why_valid: Collinear sp hybridisation leaves two independent orthogonal atomic p orbitals.

teaching_path.action: Pair each central p orbital with an adjacent carbon's parallel p orbital: C1 uses py and C3 uses pz.
teaching_path.why_valid: Pi overlap requires parallel alignment of p-orbital axes.

teaching_path.action: Deduce that terminal CH2 groups must lie in mutually perpendicular planes (90° dihedral angle) to maintain parallel pi overlap.
teaching_path.why_valid: A coplanar arrangement forces zero overlap integral (⟨py|pz⟩ = 0).

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Allene is planar because all double bonds make molecules flat.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: Why can the central carbon not use the same p orbital for both double bonds?
misconceptions.repair: A single p orbital can only overlap in one plane; two contiguous pi bonds require two orthogonal p orbitals, forcing perpendicular terminal planes.

exit_task.prompt: For 1,2-butadiene (CH3–CH=C=CH2), identify the hybridisation of each carbon and state whether the terminal substituents are in the same plane or perpendicular planes.

answer.summary: C1 is sp², C2 is sp, C3 is sp², C4 is sp³. The terminal substituents lie in mutually perpendicular planes.
reasoning: Central C2 is sp with two orthogonal p orbitals.
The cumulated double-bond triad forces perpendicular terminal planes.
answer.check: Check that C2 has 2 domains (sp) and forms orthogonal pi bonds.

oracle.no_numeric_claim: The task assesses 3D orbital deduction in a substituted cumulated polyene.

microtopics.research_contribution: Issue #36 evidence clusters Q3, Q4, and Q10 around allene orthogonal stereochemistry as the crown-jewel 3D hybridisation bottleneck.

boundary_test.prompt: If a third double bond is added (butatriene, H2C=C=C=CH2), are the terminal groups coplanar or perpendicular?
boundary_test.answer: Coplanar; with three cumulated double bonds (two sp carbons), the second twist rotates the orientation by another 90°, returning the terminal groups to coplanarity.
boundary_test.confirms: Even number of cumulated double bonds -> perpendicular terminal planes; odd number -> coplanar terminal planes.

construction_units.decision: Orient mutually perpendicular p-orbitals on central sp carbon to enforce terminal CH2 perpendicularity

microtopics.title: Delocalised pi systems and stationary resonance hybrids
microtopics.badge_reason: Translating discrete 2D Lewis resonance contributors into a single multi-centre stationary pi molecular orbital.
entry_assumptions: Can draw valid Lewis structures with resonance contributors.
microtopics.inferential_jump: A molecule with equivalent resonance structures does not oscillate between them; it possesses a single stationary electronic state with a continuous delocalised pi system and equal intermediate bond lengths.

teaching_path.action: Identify planar trigonal sigma frame (sp² hybridisation, 120° angles) for central atom in nitrate and carbonate.
Set up unhybridised 2pz orbitals on central and peripheral atoms perpendicular to the molecular plane.
teaching_path.why_valid: Parallel p-orbitals overlap sideways across all centres.

teaching_path.action: Synthesize a single 4-centre delocalised pi molecular orbital; explain why physical measurements show identical bond lengths and uniform charge distribution.
teaching_path.why_valid: Static quantum superposition replaces temporal switching.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: The molecule rapidly flips or vibrates between the three Lewis structures.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: Does spectroscopy detect different bond lengths at any moment in time?
misconceptions.repair: No; all physical measurements detect a single, symmetric species with identical bond lengths (125 pm in nitrate, 128 pm in carbonate). Resonance is a human notational construct; delocalization is physical reality.

exit_task.prompt: For planar nitrate NO3-, explain what physical observation rules out an oscillating mixture of single and double bonds.

answer.summary: X-ray crystallography and vibrational spectroscopy detect strictly identical bond lengths (125 pm) and a single D3h vibrational spectrum, whereas an oscillating mixture would show distinct single (140 pm) and double (120 pm) bond signatures.
reasoning: Identical intermediate bond lengths prove delocalization.
Spectroscopic timescale detects only a single static symmetric species.
answer.check: Compare intermediate length 125 pm with single 140 pm and double 120 pm.

oracle.no_numeric_claim: The task checks experimental falsification of oscillating resonance.

boundary_test.prompt: If carbonate CO3(2-) is protonated once to hydrogen carbonate HCO3-, are all three C-O bonds still equivalent?
boundary_test.answer: No; the O-H group localizes electron density, breaking D3h symmetry and leaving two delocalised C-O bonds and one distinct C-OH single bond.
boundary_test.confirms: Equivalent delocalisation requires equivalent peripheral atoms in symmetric positions.

compact_anchor.prompt: Resonance: rapid switching or static superposition?
compact_anchor.result: Static superposition: planar sigma frame + continuous delocalised pi system with equal bond lengths.

microtopics.title: Local hybridisation models, rotational overlap symmetry, and conjugated pathways
microtopics.badge_reason: Establishing epistemological model boundaries, rotational symmetry of sigma vs pi overlap, and conjugated vs interrupted orbital pathways.
entry_assumptions: Can assign steric numbers to central atoms and count sigma/pi bonds.
microtopics.inferential_jump: Hybridisation is an atom-centred local valence-bond model, not an entire-molecule property; bond equivalence reflects point-group symmetry, and conjugation requires an unbroken sequence of contiguous parallel p orbitals.

teaching_path.action: Establish that hybridisation is atom-specific: calculate steric number SN = sigma bonds + lone pairs for each atom individually.
teaching_path.why_valid: Molecules with heterogeneous coordination environments contain atoms with different hybridisations.

teaching_path.action: Differentiate bond overlap symmetry: sigma overlap has cylindrical symmetry (invariant under rotation), while pi overlap has directional nodal symmetry (destroyed upon twisting).
teaching_path.why_valid: Cylindrical symmetry preserves axial overlap, while lateral p overlap depends on cos θ.

teaching_path.action: Trace orbital continuity in polyenes: adjacent sp² carbons form conjugated pi pathways, whereas an intervening saturated sp³ carbon lacks a p orbital and breaks conjugation.
teaching_path.why_valid: An sp³ carbon uses all valence orbitals in localized sigma bonds, insulating adjacent pi bonds.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Assigning one hybridisation label to an entire molecule, or claiming equivalent bonds imply sp2.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: Can an entire molecule like propyne or allene have one hybridisation label?
misconceptions.repair: No; hybridisation is strictly an atomic property. In propyne, one carbon is sp3 and two are sp; in allene, two are sp2 and one is sp.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Any molecule with two double bonds is conjugated.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: Does penta-1,4-diene have continuous parallel p-orbital overlap?
misconceptions.repair: No; the central sp3 methylene carbon lacks an unhybridised p orbital, creating an electronic barrier that isolates the two double bonds.

exit_task.prompt: For 1,3-pentadiene (CH3–CH=CH–CH=CH2), identify the conjugated system and state which carbon does not participate in the conjugated pi pathway.

answer.summary: Carbons C1, C2, C3, and C4 form a 4-carbon conjugated pi system; carbon C5 (methyl, -CH3) is sp³ hybridised and does not participate.
reasoning: C1-C4 are sp² with contiguous parallel p orbitals.
C5 is saturated sp³ with no unhybridised p orbital.
answer.check: Count electron domains at each carbon atom independently.

microtopics.research_contribution: Issue #36 evidence clusters Q5, Q6, Q8, Q9, and Q10 around local model epistemics, multiple bond counting, rotational barriers, and conjugation pathways.

boundary_test.prompt: If a molecule is twisted about a single bond, does the single bond break?
boundary_test.answer: No; cylindrical symmetry maintains sigma overlap. The small barrier is purely torsional/steric, unlike double bond twisting which requires breaking the pi bond.
boundary_test.confirms: Rotational barriers in single vs double bonds have fundamentally different quantum mechanical origins.

items.title: Axial chirality in substituted allenes from orthogonal pi planes
items.prompt: Penta-2,3-diene, CH3–CH=C=CH–CH3, possesses no asymmetric tetrahedral carbon atom, yet it is a chiral molecule that can be resolved into two non-superimposable enantiomers. Using the orthogonal pi-bonding framework of allene, explain the stereochemical origin of this axial chirality. What would happen to chirality if allene were planar?
items.source_label: Original competition-style transfer problem on allene axial chirality; not claimed as an official past-paper exam question.

answer.summary: The perpendicular orientation of the terminal groups creates a chiral C2-symmetric propeller that lacks any plane or centre of symmetry when each terminal carbon carries two different substituents (–H and –CH3). If allene were planar, the entire molecule would possess a plane of symmetry (the molecular plane) and would be strictly achiral.
reasoning: In penta-2,3-diene, central C3 is sp hybridised with orthogonal py and pz orbitals.
This forces the C2–H(CH3) plane and C4–H(CH3) plane to lie at 90° to each other.
Because each terminal carbon carries two distinct groups (H ≠ CH3), the orthogonal arrangement destroys all planes of symmetry (σ) and inversion centres (i), generating axial chirality.
If allene were planar, all atoms would lie in a single reflection plane, making enantiomerism impossible.

items.title: Heats of hydrogenation and resonance stabilization in conjugated vs non-conjugated dienes
items.prompt: The heat of hydrogenation of penta-1,4-diene is approximately -254 kJ/mol (nearly double that of 1-pentene, -126 kJ/mol). In contrast, the heat of hydrogenation of buta-1,3-diene is -239 kJ/mol, which is about 15 kJ/mol less exothermic than expected for two isolated double bonds. Explain this thermodynamic difference in terms of continuous p-orbital overlap versus structural interruption by an sp³ carbon.
items.source_label: Original competition-style transfer problem on diene thermodynamic stability; not claimed as an official past-paper exam question.

answer.summary: Buta-1,3-diene has continuous parallel p-orbital overlap across all four carbons, creating a delocalised 4-centre pi molecular orbital that provides ~15 kJ/mol of resonance/conjugation stabilization energy (lowering the enthalpy of the diene). Penta-1,4-diene has an intervening sp³ methylene carbon that breaks orbital continuity, leaving two completely isolated double bonds that release the full, additive heat of two independent alkene hydrogenations.
reasoning: In buta-1,3-diene, contiguous sp² carbons permit continuous pi electron delocalisation, lowering the ground-state enthalpy by the resonance energy (~15 kJ/mol).
Hydrogenation releases less heat because the starting material is already thermodynamically stabilized.
In penta-1,4-diene, the saturated sp³ C3 carbon has no available p orbital, completely insulating the two pi bonds so no delocalisation energy exists.
